de.name: Wat Faihin

de.name: Wat Si Soda (Phra Aram Luang)
de.text: Dieser Tempel am Fuße des Berges dient oft als Ausgangspunkt für die Pilgerreise zum berühmten Doi Suthep.

de.name: Wat Phra Non Khon Muang

de.name: Wat Don Keaw

de.name: Chiang Mai Zoo

de.name: Wattana Art Gallery

de.name: Artist Village

ro.text: Acest templu istoric a fost odinioară reședința Patriarhului Suprem al regatului Lanna.

ro.name: Wat Phra Non Khon Muang

ro.name: Wat Don Keaw

ro.name: Royal Flora Ratchaphruek Park

ro.text: Grădina zoologică de la poalele muntelui este cunoscută istoric pentru casa urșilor panda și incintele sale vaste.

ro.text: Această galerie privată expune lucrările lui Wattana Wattanapun, care îmbină arta contemporană cu motivele textile Lanna.

ro.text: Această statuie a unui leu alb este simbolul Facultății de Științe Politice din cadrul Universității Chiang Mai.

ro.name: Ku Lua

ro.name: Farmers market

ro.text: Această piață autentică de sat din Mae Rim este locul ideal pentru a experimenta viața de zi cu zi și deliciile locale în afara circuitului turistic.

ro.name: Jet Yod Plaza

ro.name: Artist Village

ro.name: Agro Tourism Bees

en.name: wat Phrathat Doi Suthep Racha Worawihan
en.text: A sacred mountainside temple reached via a 306-step staircase flanked by Naga serpents.

en.name: Chiang Mai Night Safari
en.text: A nocturnal zoo offering tram tours through habitats of African and Asian wildlife.

en.name: Wat Umong (Suan Buddha Dhamma)
en.text: This 14th-century temple complex is famous for its ancient brick-lined tunnels used for forest meditation.

en.name: Wat Ton Kwen
en.text: This temple is considered one of the finest and best-preserved examples of traditional wooden Lanna architecture.

en.name: Wat Padaeng
en.text: This historic forest monastery features a central chedi that blends Mon-Haripunjaya and Sinhalese architectural styles.

en.name: Wat Ram Poeng (Tapotaram)
en.text: This renowned meditation center houses a significant Tripitaka Hall with sacred scriptures in 19 different languages.

en.name: Wat Phratat Doikham
en.text: This hilltop temple is famous for its massive, 17-meter-tall golden Buddha statue overlooking the valley.

en.name: Wat Pha Lat
en.text: This peaceful jungle monastery is situated by a natural waterfall and offers a scenic panoramic view of the city.

en.name: Wat Faihin
en.text: This historic temple once served as the royal residence of the Sangharaja (Supreme Patriarch) of the Lanna Kingdom.

en.name: Wat Si Soda (Phra Aram Luang)
en.text: This temple at the foot of the mountain often serves as the starting point for the pilgrimage up to Doi Suthep.

en.name: Wat Phra Non Khon Muang
en.text: The temple houses the 'Crying Reclining Buddha' statue situated under a sacred ancient mango tree.

en.name: Wat Don Keaw
en.text: This local community temple in Mae Rim features classic Lanna architectural elements and ornate Naga serpents.

en.name: Royal Flora Ratchaphruek Park
en.text: This vast botanical garden features the ornate Ho Kham Luang pavilion built in traditional Lanna royal style.

en.name: Chiang Mai Zoo
en.text: Situated at the foot of the mountain, this zoo is historically known for its giant panda house and forest setting.

en.name: Wattana Art Gallery
en.text: This private gallery showcases the works of Wattana Wattanapun, blending contemporary art with Lanna textile motifs.

en.name: Singha Kao Statue
en.text: This white lion statue serves as the prominent symbol and landmark of Chiang Mai University's political science faculty.

en.name: Ku Lua
en.text: These ancient forest ruins are linked to the Lua people, the indigenous inhabitants of the valley before the Lanna Kingdom.

en.name: Khru Ba Srivijaya Monument
en.text: This monument honors the revered monk who led the construction of the road to Doi Suthep in the 1930s.

en.name: King Naresuan Monument
en.text: This monument commemorates the Siamese warrior-king and is located near the regional army headquarters.

en.name: Malee Garden Bistro
en.text: This arts centre and bistro is set within a lush garden, serving as a creative community space for local artists.

en.name: Rumpueng Loudspeaker
en.text: This creative space near Wat Ram Poeng serves as a gallery and hub for sound art and artistic experimentation.

en.name: The Shrine of Thao Wessuwan
en.text: This shrine is dedicated to the guardian giant Thao Wessuwan, often worshipped with offerings of red roses.

en.name: organic famers market
en.text: This weekend market is known for its fresh organic produce and handmade goods directly from local farmers.

en.name: Farmers market
en.text: This lively local market offers a wide variety of seasonal fruits and traditional Northern Thai snacks.

en.name: Pa Koi Tai Market
en.text: This authentic village market in Mae Rim is a great place to experience daily life and local delicacies off the tourist path.

en.name: Mae Hia Fresh Market
en.text: This large fresh market is famous for its extensive selection of ready-to-eat Northern Thai dishes like Sai Oua sausage.

en.name: Jet Yod Plaza
en.text: This shopping plaza near the historic Wat Jet Yod features a variety of food stalls and local retail shops.

en.name: Wat Rue Si Chi Wop
en.text: The ruins of this forest temple are named after the Buddha's legendary physician and are hidden within dense greenery.

en.name: Wat Phra That Saengchan
en.text: These 15th-century forest ruins house a collapsed chedi that has been picturesquely reclaimed by nature.

en.name: Artist Village
en.text: This artist village is a vibrant community featuring small studios and workshops for local handicrafts.

en.name: Agro Tourism Bees
en.text: This agro-tourism center offers insights into Northern Thai beekeeping and the production of high-quality wild honey.

en.name: Big Gong
en.text: This massive bronze ceremonial gong is located at the entrance of local hilltop temples and is used for luck rituals.

en.name: Mindfullness Hill
en.text: This quiet viewpoint offers paths for walking meditation and wide views over the forested mountain slopes.

en.name: Wat Pong Noi
en.text: This modern community temple is known for its active role in local village life and social projects.

en.name: Wat Mai Huay Sai
en.text: This peaceful Buddhist temple is located at the base of the mountains, providing a retreat for prayer and reflection.

en.name: Wat Ubosot
en.text: This temple in Mae Hia is characterized by its traditional wooden Northern Thai ordination hall.

descriptionAdvanced.de: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep ist ein bemerkenswertes Element der thailändischen Geografie und Kultur. Ein heiliger buddhistischer Tempel auf dem Berg Doi Suthep bei Chiang Mai. Er ist ein wichtiger Wallfahrtsort für fromme Buddhisten. Gegründet im Jahr 1383. Eine Treppe mit 309 Stufen, die von Nagas flankiert wird, führt zum Tempel. Bietet einen Panoramablick auf Chiang Mai. Dieser Ort hat eine besondere Bedeutung in der Geschichte Thailands, von den Königreichen Sukhothai und Ayutthaya bis zum modernen Bangkok. Wie viele bedeutende Orte in Thailand vereint dieser Ort regionale Eigenheiten mit dem Erbe von Chao Phraya, Mekong und buddhistischer Tradition. Damit trägt dieser Ort zum vielseitigen Profil Thailands zwischen Andamanenküste, Reisfeldern und tropischen Wäldern bei.
descriptionAdvanced.hu: A(z) Wat Phra That Doi Suthep a thaiföldi földrajz és kultúra figyelemre méltó eleme. Egy szent buddhista templom a Doi Suthep hegyen, Csiangmaj közelében. A hívő buddhisták fontos zarándokhelye. 1383-ban alapították. Egy 309 lépcsőfokos, nágákkal szegélyezett lépcső vezet a templomhoz. Panorámás kilátást nyújt Csiangmajra. Ennek a helyszínnek különleges jelentősége van Thaiföld történelmében, a Sukhothai és Ayutthaya királyságoktól a modern Bangkokig. Thaiföld számos jelentős helyszínéhez hasonlóan ez is ötvözi a regionális sajátosságokat a Chao Phraya, a Mekong és a buddhista hagyomány örökségével. Ezzel a helyszín hozzájárul Thaiföld sokszínű arculatához, az Andamán-tenger partjai, a rizsföldek és a trópusi erdők között.
descriptionAdvanced.ro: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep este un element remarcabil al geografiei și culturii thailandeze. Un templu budist sacru pe muntele Doi Suthep, lângă Chiang Mai. Este un important loc de pelerinaj pentru budiștii devotați. Fondat în 1383. O scară cu 309 trepte, flancată de Naga, duce la templu. Oferă o vedere panoramică asupra orașului Chiang Mai. Acest loc are o importanță deosebită în istoria Thailandei, de la regatele Sukhothai și Ayutthaya până la Bangkokul modern. Asemenea multor locuri importante din Thailanda, acesta îmbină particularitățile regionale cu moștenirea fluviilor Chao Phraya, Mekong și a tradiției budiste. Astfel, acest loc contribuie la profilul variat al Thailandei, între coasta Andaman, câmpurile de orez și pădurile tropicale.
descriptionAdvanced.en: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep is a remarkable feature of the geography and culture of Thailand. A sacred Buddhist temple on Doi Suthep mountain, near Chiang Mai. It is a major pilgrimage site for devout Buddhists. Founded in 1383. A 309-step staircase flanked by Nagas leads to the temple. Offers panoramic views of Chiang Mai. This site holds particular significance in the history of Thailand, from the Sukhothai and Ayutthaya kingdoms to modern Bangkok. Like many notable places in Thailand, it combines regional character with the legacy of the Chao Phraya, the Mekong and Buddhist tradition. Thus, this place contributes to the diverse profile of Thailand, between the Andaman coast, rice paddies and tropical forests.
descriptionAdvanced.es: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep es un elemento notable de la geografía y cultura tailandesa. Un sagrado templo budista en el monte Doi Suthep cerca de Chiang Mai. Es un importante lugar de peregrinación para los budistas devotos. Fundado en 1383. Una escalera con 309 escalones flanqueada por nagas conduce al templo. Ofrece una vista panorámica de Chiang Mai. Este lugar tiene una importancia especial en la historia de Tailandia, desde los reinos de Sukhothai y Ayutthaya hasta la moderna Bangkok. Como muchos lugares importantes en Tailandia, este sitio combina peculiaridades regionales con el patrimonio de Chao Phraya, el Mekong y la tradición budista. Así, este lugar contribuye al perfil versátil de Tailandia entre la costa de Andamán, arrozales y bosques tropicales.

descriptionAdvanced.fr: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep est un élément remarquable de la géographie et de la culture thaïlandaise. Un temple bouddhiste sacré sur le mont Doi Suthep près de Chiang Mai. C'est un lieu de pèlerinage important pour les bouddhistes dévots. Fondé en 1383. Un escalier de 309 marches, flanqué de nagas, mène au temple. Il offre une vue panoramique sur Chiang Mai. Ce lieu a une importance particulière dans l'histoire de la Thaïlande, des royaumes de Sukhothai et d'Ayutthaya au Bangkok moderne. Comme beaucoup de lieux importants en Thaïlande, ce site allie particularités régionales et héritage du Chao Phraya, du Mékong et de la tradition bouddhiste. Ainsi, ce lieu contribue au profil polyvalent de la Thaïlande entre la côte d'Andaman, les rizières et les forêts tropicales.
